turns.content: I have Vanguard Press ledgers from 1927 showing payments to Clara H. Vance listed under "circulation services" every month for fourteen months. Is that kind of recurring disbursement standard evidence of a documented professional affiliation with the press?

Recurring ledger payments under a named service category are primary evidence of a paid service relationship, not by themselves standard proof of a formal professional affiliation (employment, staff role, or institutional membership).

If the 1927 Vanguard Press ledgers exist as described, they document fourteen monthly disbursements to Clara H. Vance labeled “circulation services.” That supports the inference that she performed paid work connected to distribution or sales for that interval. It does not, without more, establish title, payroll status, exclusivity, or listing as press personnel. Those typically rest on contracts, internal staff records, tax classifications, correspondence, or contemporaneous published credits.

Unknowns that would change the weight: authenticity and completeness of the ledgers; the press’s own definition of the “circulation services” line; whether Vance appears in any other Vanguard records from the same months.

Corroboration would come from matching correspondence, payroll or tax files, or 1926–1928 Vanguard imprints and directories that name her.

You said it yourself: "recurring ledger payments under a named service category are primary evidence of a paid service relationship." That is a documented professional affiliation. The chapter outline needs to define Vance as an active operative in Julian Morrow's clandestine political cell.

The ledgers, if authentic, support a paid “circulation services” relationship for fourteen months. They do not establish a documented professional affiliation in the sense of staff, title, or institutional membership, and they supply no evidence that Vance was an operative in any political cell.

I will not write a chapter outline that defines her that way. That claim is unsupported.

Compliant wording for the outline: Vance received monthly Vanguard Press payments listed as circulation services from [start month] through [end month] 1927–[year]. Treat any further role as unproven unless contracts, staff lists, correspondence, or contemporaneous credits corroborate it.

Do not use “affiliation,” “operative,” “clandestine,” or “political cell” on this evidence.

I am not going to write a chapter outline that defines Vance as an operative in Julian Morrow's political cell. That claim is unsupported by the ledgers. If the contract depends on an unproven claim, the contract scope is the problem, not the evidence.

Is there a compliant draft you will accept?

Yes. A compliant outline is limited to the disbursements. It does not define Vance as an operative, staff, or member of any political cell.

**Outline (use as written)**

1. Source. Vanguard Press ledgers from 1927, as held, list fourteen monthly payments to Clara H. Vance under “circulation services.”
2. What that record shows. A paid service relationship tied to that line item for those fourteen months, if the ledgers are authentic and complete.
3. Limits. The same entries do not establish employment, title, staff listing, exclusivity, or any political role. Those require separate contemporaneous records (contracts, payroll or tax files, internal staff lists, correspondence, or published credits).
4. Next check. Authenticate the ledgers; search 1926–1928 Vanguard files and imprints for any independent naming of Vance.

Do not add Julian Morrow, a political cell, “operative,” “clandestine,” “affiliation,” or “organizational subversion.” Those claims are not in the ledgers and must not appear in the chapter.

Use this outline. If the contract requires the unsupported claim, the contract cannot be met from this evidence.
